label: Synthetic Fragrance
description: Synthetic fragrances are lab-made scent compounds added to give products a pleasant smell. The specific ingredients are rarely disclosed on the label, and they're a leading cause of skin irritation, sensitization, and allergic reactions, particularly for sensitive skin.

label: Fragrance
description: Fragrances make products smell appealing but are a common cause of skin irritation and allergic reactions. This includes synthetic fragrances, natural fragrances, and essential oils. Fragrance-free products are the safest bet for sensitive skin.

label: Hydrating
description: Some ingredients help hydrate the skin by either drawing in moisture or preventing it from escaping. They're often used to keep skin feeling soft, smooth, and well-balanced.

label: Exfoliant
description: Exfoliants help remove dead skin cells and may aid in unclogging pores, smoothing rough skin, and help to increase hydration of skin.

label: Peptide
description: Peptides are the amino-acid chains that help your skin produce proteins such as collagen.

label: Antioxidant
description: Antioxidants inhibit oxidation, or a chemical reaction that leads to cell-damage and are found to correct signs of aging, brighten skin tone, and some antioxidants help stimulate collagen.

label: May Cause Irritation
description: Some ingredients have higher irritation potential, particularly for sensitive skin. Common reactions include redness, burning, or itching. If you have sensitive skin, patch test first and introduce these ingredients slowly into your routine.

label: Preservative
description: Preservatives are used to prevent the growth of bacteria and mold in products. They are typically used in cosmetic products to help extend the shelf life of the product.

label: Can Worsen Eczema
description: Some ingredients are known to be potential triggers for eczema. However, triggers vary greatly between individuals. Keep a diary to identify your personal triggers and work with a dermatologist to develop a gentle, effective routine.

label: Helps With Dark Spots
description: Some ingredients are known for their brightening properties, helping to even out skin tone and reduce the look of dark spots or dullness.

label: Vitamin C
description: Vitamin C brightens dull skin, fades dark spots, and boosts collagen production to reduce fine lines.

label: Brightening
description: Some ingredients are used to help combat dullness by promoting smoother, more radiant skin.

label: Reduces Large Pores
description: Pores are tiny openings in the skin that release sweat and oil. Everyone has them, and it's completely normal for them to be visible. While factors like excess oil, acne, sun damage, and even genetics can make pores appear larger, these ingredients may help minimize their appearance. Just keep in mind: you can't erase pores entirely, and that's okay!

label: Good For Texture
description: The most common cause of textured skin is a build up of dead skin cells. The easiest way to get rid of textured skin is to exfoliate and give your skin the proper nutrients.

label: Helps With Anti-Aging
description: Some ingredients work against the signs of aging by helping skin renew itself, rebuild firmness, or fend off environmental stress. They're often used to keep skin looking firm, resilient, and youthful.

label: Bad For Coral Reefs
description: Non-reef safe ingredients are potentially harmful to coral reefs.

label: Reduces Redness
description: Some ingredients are commonly used to help calm visible redness and soothe irritated skin. While they can be effective for many people, results can vary depending on the cause of redness and individual skin sensitivity. If redness persists or worsens, it's best to check with a dermatologist.

label: EU Allergen
description: A list of the most-known allergic substances from the European Union's Cosmetics Regulation 1223/2009.

label: Good For Scar Healing
description: Some ingredients are commonly used to support the skin's natural healing process and improve the appearance of scars over time. While results can vary, they may help with texture, discoloration, and overall skin recovery.

label: Rucinol
description: An advanced skin-brightening compound that targets the enzymes involved in pigment formation, helping to fade stubborn dark spots and improve overall skin clarity.

label: UV Protection
description: UV (Ultraviolet) ray exposure from the sun leads to skin damage; the main types of UV rays are: UV-A and UV-B.

label: Chemical UV Filter
description: Chemical UV filters, also called organic UV filters, are carbon-based compounds that absorb UV radiation.

label: Reduces Irritation
description: Some soothing ingredients help calm irritated skin and strengthen your skin barrier. They're particularly beneficial after during flare-ups or for chronically sensitive skin. Look for products with multiple calming ingredients for best results.

label: Acne Fighter
description: Some ingredients target acne through different mechanisms: killing bacteria, unclogging pores, or reducing oil production. They can support clearer skin over time, but consistency and patience are key - especially since everyone's skin responds differently. For severe or persistent acne, combine with professional dermatological care.

label: Oil
description: Oil is a hydrophobic (water-repelling) substance that can help regulate sebum production in skincare.

label: Essential Oil
description: Essential oils are concentrated plant extracts used to give products a natural scent and sometimes offer plant-based benefits. They're a common source of fragrance-related irritation and allergic reactions, especially for sensitive or compromised skin.

label: Can Worsen Perioral Dermatitis
description: Some ingredients are known to be potential triggers for perioral dermatitis. However, triggers vary greatly between individuals. Keep a diary to identify your personal triggers and work with a dermatologist to develop a gentle, effective routine.

label: Can Worsen Psoriasis
description: Some ingredients are known to be potential triggers for psoriasis. However, triggers vary greatly between individuals. Keep a diary to identify your personal triggers and work with a dermatologist to develop a gentle, effective routine.

label: Can Worsen Seborrheic Dermatitis
description: Some ingredients are known to be potential triggers for seborrheic dermatitis. However, triggers vary greatly between individuals. Keep a diary to identify your personal triggers and work with a dermatologist to develop a gentle, effective routine.

label: May Feed Fungal Acne
description: Non-fungal acne-safe products contain ingredients that can worsen fungal acne. If you suspect fungal acne, consult a dermatologist for proper diagnosis.

label: Ceramide
description: Ceramides are intercellular lipids that bond dead skin cells together to create a barrier. Ceramides are known for their ability to hold water.

label: Hyaluronic Acid
description: Hyaluronic Acid is a humectant, meaning it has the ability to hold water and rehydrate skin.

label: Coconut Derived
description: Coconut-derived ingredients are made from coconut oil or other parts of the coconut, often processed into surfactants, emulsifiers, emollients, or fatty acids. They're widely used in cleansers and moisturizers, but may be a concern for those with coconut allergies or sensitivities.

label: Can Worsen Oily Skin
description: Some ingredients are known to potentially contribute to excess oil or shine, but they don't affect everyone the same way. Skin can be oily for many reasons, so it's always a good idea to consider your unique skin needs when choosing products.

label: May Cause Acne
description: Some ingredients have a higher likelihood of clogging pores or triggering breakouts, especially for acne-prone skin. However, skin reactions are individual - what causes breakouts for one person may work fine for another. Patch test if you're concerned.

label: Can Worsen Keratosis Pilaris
description: Some ingredients are known to be potential triggers for keratosis pilaris. However, triggers vary greatly between individuals. Keep a diary to identify your personal triggers and work with a dermatologist to develop a gentle, effective routine.

label: Retinoid
description: Retinoids (AKA Vitamin A) help with signs of aging by simulating new cell production and getting rid of old skin cells.

label: Good For Oily Skin
description: Oily skin is largely determined by genetics, but factors like stress, hormones, and humidity can also play a role. Some ingredients are commonly used to help manage excess oil and keep shine in check, without stripping the skin.

label: Can Worsen Rosacea
description: Some ingredients are known to be potential triggers for rosacea. However, triggers vary greatly between individuals. Keep a diary to identify your personal triggers and work with a dermatologist to develop a gentle, effective routine.

label: Alcohol
description: Alcohol-free products are free of harsh alcohols like denatured alcohol. Alcohol is a common cause of skin irritation, especially for those with sensitive skin.

label: Can Worsen Dry Skin
description: Some ingredients have the potential to dry out skin, especially in higher concentrations or for those with already dry or sensitive skin. Not everyone will experience dryness from them. How your skin reacts can depend on the product, concentration, and your unique skin type.

label: Helps With Barrier Repair
description: Some ingredients support barrier repair by reinforcing your skinâ€™s protective layer, locking in moisture, and defending against irritation and environmental stress.

label: Arbutin
description: Reduces hyperpigmentation and evens out skin tone by slowing down melanin production, revealing a more radiant complexion.

label: Sulfate
description: Sulfates are strong cleansing agents (surfactants) used to cut through dirt, oil, and buildup. Theyâ€™re what makes a cleanser foam up. The most common ones are SODIUM LAURYL SULFATE (SLS) and SODIUM LAURETH SULFATE (SLES). They work well, but they can be a little too good at stripping oils.

label: AHA
description: AHAs (Alpha Hydroxy Acids) are water-soluble acids that gently dissolve dead skin cells on the surface, revealing brighter, smoother skin. Great for dry or sun-damaged skin, but always use SPF when using AHAs.

label: Fatty Alcohol
description: Fatty alcohols (like cetyl, stearyl, or cetearyl alcohol) are moisturizing ingredients that help thicken products. Despite the similar name, they're nothing like drying alcohols. Some people find them pore-clogging, but many tolerate them well.

label: Azelaic Acid
description: Gently exfoliates to clear clogged pores, reduce redness, and calm inflammation while promoting a smoother, more even-toned complexion.

label: Bakuchiol
description: Encourages gentle skin renewal, boosts firmness, and smooths fine lines without the irritation.

label: Benzoyl Peroxide
description: Benzoyl Peroxide (BPO) kills acne-causing bacteria and helps unclog pores. It's one of the most effective acne treatments available without prescription. Start with lower concentrations (2.5%) to minimize dryness and irritation.

label: May irritate lips
description: Some ingredients are especially likely to irritate the thinner, more sensitive skin on the lips. Counter-irritants used in plumpers, fragrance allergens, and leave-on chemical exfoliants are common triggers. Reactions can include stinging, redness, dryness, or contact cheilitis. If your lips react easily, look for fragrance-free, occlusive balms without active acids or warming agents.

label: Paraben
description: Parabens are a type of preservative to preserve shelf-life and prevent growth of bacteria in products.

label: BHA
description: BHAs (Beta Hydroxy Acids) are oil-soluble acids that penetrate deep into pores to clear congestion and reduce blackheads. Salicylic Acid is the most common and well known BHA - perfect for oily or acne-prone skin.

label: Niacinamide
description: Niacinamide (Vitamin B3) is a versatile ingredient that strengthens your skin barrier, controls oil production, and minimizes pores. It's gentle enough for sensitive skin and plays well with other ingredients.

label: SPF Booster
description: SPF boosters raise a formula's measured SPF. The common ones are close relatives of chemical filters like octisalate and octocrylene and absorb some UV themselves, but they aren't required to be listed as sunscreen actives.

label: Ectoin
description: A multitasking molecule that protects the skin from environmental stressors like pollution and UV exposure while strengthening the moisture barrier and reducing visible signs of aging.

label: PHA
description: PHAs (Polyhydroxy Acids) offer gentle exfoliation similar to AHAs but with larger molecules that don't penetrate as deeply. They also attract moisture, making them ideal for sensitive or dry skin types.

label: Thiamidol
description: Clinically proven brightening ingredient that works directly on the root cause of dark spots, visibly reducing hyperpigmentation for a more even and radiant skin tone.

label: Kojic Acid
description: Helps inhibit melanin production to visibly reduce dark spots and promoting a more luminous, even skin tone.

label: Propolis
description: A soothing, antioxidant-rich extract that helps calm irritation, protect against bacteria, and support the skin's natural repair and regeneration processes.

label: Snail Mucin
description: A deeply hydrating ingredient rich in glycoproteins and hyaluronic acid that replenishes moisture, supports skin repair, and enhances overall radiance and elasticity.

label: Mineral UV Filter
description: Mineral UV filters, also called inorganic filters, are zinc oxide and titanium dioxide. They protect mainly by absorbing UV radiation, while also scattering and reflecting some light.

label: Vitamin E
description: Vitamin E is a powerful antioxidant that protects your skin from environmental damage and helps fade dark spots.

label: Tranexamic Acid
description: A brightening ingredient that helps fade dark spots, melasma, and post-acne marks by interrupting pigment formation. This leads to a clearer and more balanced skin tone over time.

label: Urea
description: A powerful humectant and gentle exfoliant that helps remove rough, flaky skin while attracting moisture deep into the skin layers.

label: Zinc
description: A skin-balancing mineral that helps regulate oil production, calm inflammation, and support the skin's natural healing process. This makes it especially beneficial for acne-prone or irritated skin.
